campaign.name: Q2 product launch
campaign.product: Keelstone, an AI workplace safety platform for mid-market employers in high-injury industries. It runs on the cameras a site already has to flag unsafe lifts, slips and near-misses, turns them into crew coaching, automates OSHA paperwork, and gives the CFO and broker a data-backed risk story at renewal.

variants.name: Variant A
variants.headline: Lower your workers' comp premium.
variants.message: Lower your workers' comp premium. Our AI finds the risks driving your claims so you can bring your experience mod down before renewal.
variants.rationale: Creative brief direction 1 (cost). Speaks to the CFO's premium and mod. Avoids the unproven 20% premium claim and names the real path: the mod at renewal.

variants.name: Variant B
variants.headline: Fewer injuries. Fewer claims.
variants.message: Fewer injuries. Fewer claims. Spot unsafe lifts, falls and near-misses on the cameras you already have, so your safety team can coach before someone gets hurt.
variants.rationale: Direction 2 (safety). Leads with the proposition's first half and the cameras-you-already-have mandatory. Written for the safety manager.

variants.name: Variant C
variants.headline: Give your broker better data.
variants.message: Give your broker better data. We turn what's happening on your sites into the risk story carriers want to see, so you and your broker walk into renewal with leverage.
variants.rationale: Direction 3 (partnership). Puts the broker beside the employer at renewal, as the brief requires.

stress.claim: Customers cut their workers' comp premium by 20% in the first year.

attacks.attack: Premiums are set by the carrier against the experience mod, and the mod looks back three years. Nobody controls a 20% cut in year one, and if my client expects it, I'm the one explaining why it didn't happen.
attacks.evidence_needed: Mod and premium history for named customers, with the renewal year the change actually hit.

attacks.attack: If the company is saving 20% on insurance, it's coming from somewhere. Usually it means fighting our claims harder.
attacks.evidence_needed: A clear statement that footage is used for coaching, not discipline, ideally agreed with workers.

attacks.attack: Nobody on the floor cares about the premium. If this is sold as a cost-cutting tool, people will treat it like one and work around it.
attacks.evidence_needed: Worker-facing language about safety outcomes, and a pilot crew who'll vouch for it.

attacks.attack: First-year premium cuts are rare. The usual path is fewer claims, then a better mod a year or two later. Promising 20% up front makes the whole pitch look naive, and it makes me look naive if I bring it to a client.
attacks.evidence_needed: Claim frequency in year one, then the mod and premium changes that followed.

attacks.attack: Before anyone talks savings, tell me what runs on our network and where the video goes. If security says no, the 20% is irrelevant.
attacks.evidence_needed: Architecture diagram, data retention policy, SOC 2 report.

stress.rewrite: Customers cut claim frequency in the first year, and that shows up in the experience mod at the next renewal. Bring your broker. We'll show you the loss runs.
stress.rewrite_rationale: The original promise fails the top attack: carriers set premiums against a three-year mod, so nobody controls a 20% cut in year one. The rewrite claims what the product controls (claim frequency), names the real path to premium (the mod at renewal), and brings the broker in instead of going around them.

transcript.text: We help employers lower their workers' comp premium. Our AI finds the risks driving your claims so you can bring your experience mod down.

Our mod is the reason I took this call. But I've had three vendors tell me that this year. What's the actual number, and when do I see it? Premium savings show up at renewal. Your invoice shows up next month.
Most customers see claim frequency drop in the first six months, and that shows up in the mod over the next renewal cycle.
So, eighteen months to two years before it shows up in my premium. That's fine, if you'll put it in writing. Who else in transportation is using it, and can I call their CFO?
Yes, we can set up a reference call. What would you need to see before taking it to your CEO?
A payback model with our own loss runs in it, not a generic slide. And I'd want our broker in the room. If they don't buy it, I won't get it past the board.

brief.summary: Keelstone, an AI workplace safety platform for mid-market employers in high-injury industries. It runs on the cameras a site already has to flag unsafe lifts, slips and near-misses, turns them into crew coaching, automates OSHA paperwork, and gives the CFO and broker a data-backed risk story at renewal.
brief.target: Mid-market employers (50 to 5,000 employees) in high-injury industries, buying through an independent broker.
brief.proposition: Fewer injuries, fewer claims, and a better story at renewal, on the cameras you already have.
brief.tone: Plain, practical and specific. Talk like a safety professional, not a tech company. Never fear-based.
mandatories: Position the broker as a partner, never as someone we go around.
Only use claims we can prove (MRD proof table).
Mention the cameras you already have in at least one direction.

features.name: Hazard detection on existing cameras
features.description: Flags unsafe lifts, slips, missing PPE and forklift near-misses on existing IP cameras. Alerts go to the safety team.

features.name: Crew coaching feed
features.description: Weekly coaching clips from flagged events, faces blurred, played in toolbox talks.

features.name: Broker risk report
features.description: Renewal-ready report of hazard trends and corrective actions. Brokers see all their Keelstone clients.

features.name: Total cost of risk dashboard
features.description: Premium, claims, reserves and lost workdays in one view, with an ROI tracker against the customer's baseline.

features.name: OSHA recordkeeping automation
features.description: Drafts OSHA 300, 300A and 301 entries from incident reports, with an audit trail.

features.name: Privacy and data controls
features.description: Edge blurring, 30-day video retention, SSO, role-based access, coaching-only video policy.

features.name: Anonymous near-miss reporting
features.description: Workers report a hazard from their phone in under 30 seconds, anonymously if they choose.

features.name: Claims and HRIS integrations
features.description: Payroll, HRIS and carrier claims feeds flow in without manual exports. Needs IT approval.

claims.proof: Pilot of 6 customers, 12 months, internal analysis.
